title.source: CamelBak水背上身，為何出口還得受咬？｜品牌故事
title.text: CamelBak: water on your back—why bite the outlet? | Brand Stories

description.source:
一袋水背上身以後，怎麼讓它在要喝時出來，其他時候留在該在的地方？從品牌回顧的襪子與衣夾，循著口器原件、2006展場水瓶、2015實驗室觀測、2016工程師回述，再走到現行補水密封與乾燥。原型賽事1988/1989原主辦回顧同段矛盾，不擇一；公司成立1989另屬事件。專利方案、商品觀測與各期樣件不混成同一SKU、批次或歷史首次；測試動作不等耐久結果。畫面為原創匿名概念插圖，尚未生成媒體。

description.text:
Once water is on your back, how do you get it out when you want a drink and keep it in place otherwise? Follow the brand's sock-and-clothespin account through a mouthpiece patent, a bottle at a 2006 trade show, a 2015 lab report, a 2016 engineer's recollection, and current sealing and drying guidance. The race organizer's retrospective gives conflicting 1988/1989 dates; neither is selected. The company's 1989 founding is a separate event. Patent designs, observed products and samples from different periods are not treated as one SKU, batch or historical first. Test procedures are not durability results. Visuals are original anonymous concept illustrations; media has not yet been generated.

c14r1h01: 你背著三公升水，若管口一直滴，
喝到以前就先漏掉；多裝水，能解決這件事嗎？
c14r1h02: 八〇年代末，德州一場單車賽裡，
品牌回顧中的艾德森，把一袋水放到車衣背後。
c14r1o05: 這套拼裝留下的，是手動夾閉：衣夾還要有人照顧，
並不會因為你喝完，就自己回到管口。
c14r1v01: 後來的咬閥，把這個開關問題交給了嘴；
其中一份口器專利，記下可變形的出口。
c14r1v02: 這份申請在一九九八年提出，二〇〇〇年獲准；
它描述的出口，不是一個始終敞開的圓孔。
c14r1v03: 前端兩片相貼的部分，合起一條平常閉著的狹縫；
水路已經接上，縫卻還沒打開。
c14r1v04: 你若只想到把孔挖大，就漏掉了這個問題：
不喝的時候，那個孔由誰補回去？
c14r1v05: 專利裡，牙齒壓住可咬的區域，口器變形，
貼在一起的兩片才分開，形成出水口。
c14r1v06: 力氣撤掉以後，彈性讓它回到閉合狀態；
開和關，靠的是同一個零件的形變。
c14r1v09: 文件選材看的是能不能回到閉合狀態，
並舉一種硬度的矽膠作例子；軟，還得能回彈。
c14r1v10: 口器的脖子接著管端，頭部留給嘴含住；
那個整天碰到嘴的地方，怎麼清理？
c14r1v14: 用的是圖一到圖十那種口器，放進嘴裡、
咬到出水狀態，再像吸管那樣吸水。
c14r1v15: 專利申請人自報的流量，是每秒約三十五到四十五毫升；
數字裡，也包含人在吸的動作。
c14r1v16: 我讀這段時，最在意的是水路終於有了可觀察的結果：
嘴一邊開口，一邊把水吸過來。
c14r1v17: 這是那個設計記載的測試，還不是每一款袋子、
每一個嘴，都會流出同樣的量。
c14r1b03: 你手裡換回瓶子，嘴邊卻不用換回一個敞開的瓶口；
這才是讓我停下來看的地方。
c14r1b06: 同年公開的一份水瓶申請文件，
描述了受壓變形的咬口，也引用先前那份口器專利。
c14r1b07: 裡面的構想仍是壓開、撤力回閉；
換容器，不必連開關的原理都從頭換掉。
c14r1b09: 防漏，是公司在報導裡的說法；這個展品，
讓出口和容器的分工，出現在日常水瓶裡。
c14r1b11: 不過，瓶子拿起一次能喝，和袋子在身上反覆擠、
反覆咬，能算同一場考驗嗎？
c14r1t01: 背袋會受擠壓，水路也分成不同部件；
二〇一四年年報，寫下當時的組合。
c14r1t02: 那是聚氨酯袋體、管子，再接自封口器；
同份年報的採購段，也列出聚氨酯膜。
c14r1t05: 二〇一五年，記者走進加州佩塔盧馬的實驗室，
看見水袋正在被壓、被扭。
c14r1t06: 開場那副金屬牙齒，是兩片金屬夾著十二個咬閥，
反覆模擬大人和孩子的咬壓。
c14r1t11: 而螢幕上的咬口形狀，還不是你能碰到的軟零件；
工程師先怎麼把它做出來？
c14r1m01: 二〇一六年的供應商個案，訪問了設計工程師麥克里迪；
他做的是一體、自封的矽膠咬閥樣件。
c14r1m09: 可是，就算你嘴邊的咬口會自封，
補水時還有另一個開口必須打開；那裡也能守住水嗎？
c14r1r01: 補水口把你帶回袋子上；開場那款水袋的現行介紹，
特別列了方便握住、重新灌水的把手。
c14r1r03: 我原先容易把不漏水，全想成嘴邊那一小塊；
可是補水蓋，也是一個得關好的接面。
c14r1r05: 原廠現行問答列出兩個可能原因：
蓋子螺紋有砂粒，或者蓋內的密封圈扭了。
c14r1r06: 砂粒讓蓋子不能完整密合；
那個黑色環若扭曲變形，也會破壞蓋口的密封。
c14r1r11: 我覺得，它沒有離開一開始的問題：讓水跟你走，
還得知道它有沒有從別的地方先走掉。
c14r1d01: 洗後殘水，把水路反過來考了一次；
原廠清潔頁說，角落、飲水管和咬口都可能留水。
c14r1d03: 我覺得這是整段水路最刁鑽的反面：
喝的時候要留住水，收起來以前，卻要把殘水送走。
c14r1d04: 原廠的清洗範圍，因此不只是一個大袋子；
水走過的管與咬口，也得接到清水。
c14r1d06: 清潔頁給的動作，是把袋體撐開，讓內部通風；
乾燥架把兩邊內壁分開，也讓水能排出。
c14r1d08: 飲水管若緊緊盤起來，原廠說水可能積在低處；
怎麼讓管內也有乾燥的路？
c14r1d10: 分件晾乾用到的是可拆零件；管與咬口各自留出的空間，
也讓你能查看裡面是不是還有水。
c14r1d12: 原廠要求收存前再看接縫、角落、管子和接口，
有沒有水滴或凝結；還有水，就繼續晾乾。
c14r1d13: 開場問水能不能留在該在的地方，到這裡，
答案多了一個時間點：收起來時，它得離開。
c14r1ct1: 一袋水的方便，是把開、關與重新使用接成水路；
容量留在背上，出口和接縫，卻都得被照顧。
c14r1ct2: 你最常把水帶去騎車、走路，還是放在桌邊？
留言告訴我，哪個小地方最讓你在意。
c14r1ct3: 想知道熟悉的物品，怎麼把方便送到你手裡，
歡迎訂閱，和我一起看那些真正起作用的小動作。

lines.source: 你背著三公升水，若管口一直滴，喝到以前就先漏掉；多裝水，能解決這件事嗎？
lines.text: You carry three liters of water, but if the tube keeps dripping, it leaks away before you drink. Can carrying more water solve that?

lines.source: 八〇年代末，德州一場單車賽裡，品牌回顧中的艾德森，把一袋水放到車衣背後。
lines.text: In the late 1980s, at a Texas bike race, Eidson put a bag of water behind his cycling jersey, according to the brand's retrospective.

lines.source: 袋子外面套著襪子，管子越過肩膀；我注意到的，卻是管口那枚衣夾。
lines.text: A sock covered the bag, and a tube ran over his shoulder. What caught my eye was the clothespin at the tube's end.

lines.source: 後來，出口被夾在模擬牙齒的金屬之間。
lines.text: Later, the outlet was clamped between metal pieces that simulated teeth.

lines.source: 另一份個案裡，工程師為咬口做出模具。
lines.text: In another case study, an engineer made a mold for the mouthpiece.

lines.source: 今天跟著CamelBak的一袋水，從背上身，走到下一次還能再喝。
lines.text: Today, follow a bag of CamelBak water from carrying it on your back to being able to drink from it again next time.

lines.source: 把水背上身之後，怎麼讓它在你要喝時出來，其他時候留在該在的地方？
lines.text: Once water is on your back, how do you let it out when you want a drink and keep it where it belongs the rest of the time?

lines.source: 我讀的紐西蘭品牌回顧裡，艾德森用那枚衣夾，夾住了管子出口。
lines.text: In the brand's New Zealand retrospective I read, Eidson used that clothespin to clamp the tube's outlet.

lines.source: 他是急救醫療技術員，回顧裡那袋水，用的原是點滴袋。
lines.text: He was an emergency medical technician. The water bag in that account had originally been an IV bag.

lines.source: 但把出口移到嘴邊，和讓出口自己關上，是同一件事嗎？
lines.text: But is moving the outlet to your mouth the same as making it close itself?

lines.source: 這套拼裝留下的，是手動夾閉：衣夾還要有人照顧，並不會因為你喝完，就自己回到管口。
lines.text: This improvised setup still needed manual clamping. Someone had to handle the clothespin; it would not return to the tube simply because you finished drinking.

lines.source: 如果放開嘴，出口就能關回去，你的手是不是能少管一件事？
lines.text: If the outlet closed when you released it from your mouth, would your hands have one less thing to manage?

lines.source: 後來的咬閥，把這個開關問題交給了嘴；其中一份口器專利，記下可變形的出口。
lines.text: Later bite valves gave the mouth control of that switch. One mouthpiece patent records a deformable outlet.

lines.source: 這份申請在一九九八年提出，二〇〇〇年獲准；它描述的出口，不是一個始終敞開的圓孔。
lines.text: The application was filed in 1998 and granted in 2000. Its outlet is not a round hole that stays open all the time.

lines.source: 前端兩片相貼的部分，合起一條平常閉著的狹縫；水路已經接上，縫卻還沒打開。
lines.text: Two touching sections at the front form a normally closed slit. The water path is connected, but the slit has not opened.

lines.source: 你若只想到把孔挖大，就漏掉了這個問題：不喝的時候，那個孔由誰補回去？
lines.text: If you only think about making the hole bigger, you miss a question: who closes that hole when you are not drinking?

lines.source: 專利裡，牙齒壓住可咬的區域，口器變形，貼在一起的兩片才分開，形成出水口。
lines.text: In the patent, teeth press the bite region, deforming the mouthpiece. The two touching sections separate to form an outlet.

lines.source: 力氣撤掉以後，彈性讓它回到閉合狀態；開和關，靠的是同一個零件的形變。
lines.text: When that force is removed, elasticity returns it to a closed state. Opening and closing rely on the same part changing shape.

lines.source: 我喜歡這個轉換：原先掛在外面的衣夾，換成出口本身會回復的形狀。
lines.text: I like that change: the external clothespin gives way to a shape within the outlet that returns by itself.

lines.source: 可是，材料軟到能咬，為什麼不會放開以後，就一直扁在那裡？
lines.text: But if the material is soft enough to bite, why doesn't it stay flattened after you let go?

lines.source: 文件選材看的是能不能回到閉合狀態，並舉一種硬度的矽膠作例子；軟，還得能回彈。
lines.text: The document selects material for its ability to return to a closed state and gives silicone of a particular hardness as an example. It must be soft yet spring back.

lines.source: 口器的脖子接著管端，頭部留給嘴含住；那個整天碰到嘴的地方，怎麼清理？
lines.text: The mouthpiece's neck connects to the tube, and its head goes in your mouth. How do you clean the bit that touches your mouth all day?

lines.source: 專利說，口器能從管子上滑下來，再裝回去，方便清潔與維護。
lines.text: The patent says the mouthpiece can slide off the tube and be put back on, making cleaning and maintenance easier.

lines.source: 文件裡還記了一組出水測試；咬開這條縫，水究竟能怎樣通過？
lines.text: The document also records a flow test. Once you bite open this slit, how can water pass through?

lines.source: 用的是圖一到圖十那種口器，放進嘴裡、咬到出水狀態，再像吸管那樣吸水。
lines.text: It uses the mouthpiece shown in Figures 1 through 10: put it in your mouth, bite it into the flow position, then suck as if through a straw.

lines.source: 專利申請人自報的流量，是每秒約三十五到四十五毫升；數字裡，也包含人在吸的動作。
lines.text: The patent applicant reports a flow of about 35 to 45 milliliters per second. That figure includes the user's sucking action.

lines.source: 我讀這段時，最在意的是水路終於有了可觀察的結果：嘴一邊開口，一邊把水吸過來。
lines.text: What interests me most here is that the water path finally has an observable result: the mouth opens the outlet while drawing water through it.

lines.source: 這是那個設計記載的測試，還不是每一款袋子、每一個嘴，都會流出同樣的量。
lines.text: This is the test recorded for that design. It does not mean every bag and every mouthpiece will deliver the same flow.

lines.source: 可既然控制已經在嘴邊，水還非得背在背後嗎？
lines.text: But with control now at your mouth, does the water still have to stay on your back?

lines.source: 二〇〇六年的展場報導裡，那個咬著喝的出口，已經搬到透明水瓶上。
lines.text: In a 2006 trade-show report, that bite-to-drink outlet had moved onto a clear water bottle.

lines.source: 記者寫的是七百五十毫升瓶，咬口可以翻起，下面接著瓶內一小段吸管。
lines.text: The reporter describes a 750-milliliter bottle with a flip-up bite valve and a short straw connected beneath it inside the bottle.

lines.source: 你手裡換回瓶子，嘴邊卻不用換回一個敞開的瓶口；這才是讓我停下來看的地方。
lines.text: You have a bottle in your hand again, without returning to an open bottle mouth. That is what made me pause.

lines.source: 容器變了，讓出口在喝的時候打開，這個工作能一起搬過去嗎？
lines.text: The container has changed. Can the job of opening only when you drink move with it?

lines.source: 同年公開的一份水瓶申請文件，描述了受壓變形的咬口，也引用先前那份口器專利。
lines.text: A bottle application published that same year describes a bite mouthpiece that deforms under pressure and cites the earlier mouthpiece patent.

lines.source: 裡面的構想仍是壓開、撤力回閉；換容器，不必連開關的原理都從頭換掉。
lines.text: Its idea is still to press open and release to close. Changing the container need not mean starting over with the switching principle.

lines.source: 可是，報導說它防漏，是記者測過，還是公司這樣說？
lines.text: But when the report calls it leakproof, did the reporter test that, or was it the company's claim?

lines.source: 防漏，是公司在報導裡的說法；這個展品，讓出口和容器的分工，出現在日常水瓶裡。
lines.text: Leakproof was the company's description in the report. This exhibit brought the division of work between outlet and container to an everyday bottle.

lines.source: 不過，瓶子拿起一次能喝，和袋子在身上反覆擠、反覆咬，能算同一場考驗嗎？
lines.text: Still, is drinking once from a bottle the same test as repeatedly squeezing a bag on your body and biting its valve?

lines.source: 背袋會受擠壓，水路也分成不同部件；二〇一四年年報，寫下當時的組合。
lines.text: A carried bag gets squeezed, and the water path has separate parts. The 2014 annual report describes that period's combination.

lines.source: 那是聚氨酯袋體、管子，再接自封口器；同份年報的採購段，也列出聚氨酯膜。
lines.text: It was a polyurethane reservoir, a tube and a self-sealing mouthpiece. The same report also lists polyurethane film in its procurement section.

lines.source: 你背著它走時，會彎動的是袋子，嘴邊一再受壓的，卻是另一個小部件。
lines.text: As you carry it, the bag bends, while a different small part at your mouth is repeatedly compressed.

lines.source: 所以，要看反覆使用，該把力氣加在哪裡？
lines.text: So, to examine repeated use, where should the force be applied?

lines.source: 二〇一五年，記者走進加州佩塔盧馬的實驗室，看見水袋正在被壓、被扭。
lines.text: In 2015, a reporter visited the lab in Petaluma, California, and saw reservoirs being compressed and twisted.

lines.source: 開場那副金屬牙齒，是兩片金屬夾著十二個咬閥，反覆模擬大人和孩子的咬壓。
lines.text: The metal teeth from the opening were two metal pieces clamping 12 bite valves, repeatedly simulating bites by adults and children.

lines.source: 我覺得這個畫面，比一句耐用更值得細看。
lines.text: I think that scene deserves a closer look than a simple claim of durability.

lines.source: 而螢幕上的咬口形狀，還不是你能碰到的軟零件；工程師先怎麼把它做出來？
lines.text: But the mouthpiece shape on a screen is not yet a soft part you can touch. How does an engineer first make it?

lines.source: 二〇一六年的供應商個案，訪問了設計工程師麥克里迪；他做的是一體、自封的矽膠咬閥樣件。
lines.text: A 2016 supplier case study interviewed design engineer McCready. He was making a one-piece, self-sealing silicone bite-valve sample.

lines.source: 開場那副模具，是他用三維列印做的，再用來製作矽膠咬閥樣件。
lines.text: The mold from our opening was one he made by 3D printing, then used to produce silicone bite-valve samples.

lines.source: 工程師回述，這樣兩天就拿到了測試零件。
lines.text: The engineer recalled getting test parts this way in just two days.

lines.source: 我更想知道，拿到軟樣件後，工程師還想取得什麼？
lines.text: I am more interested in what the engineer wanted to obtain after getting those soft samples.

lines.source: 他說，越能從真人測試取得回饋越好。
lines.text: He said the more feedback they could get from testing with real people, the better.

lines.source: 可是，就算你嘴邊的咬口會自封，補水時還有另一個開口必須打開；那裡也能守住水嗎？
lines.text: But even if the valve at your mouth seals itself, another opening must open for refilling. Can that one keep water in too?

lines.source: 補水口把你帶回袋子上；開場那款水袋的現行介紹，特別列了方便握住、重新灌水的把手。
lines.text: The refill opening brings you back to the bag. The current description of the reservoir from our opening specifically lists a handle for easy gripping and refilling.

lines.source: 這一款另有單手開關，讓你用一隻手關住飲水管。
lines.text: This model also has an on/off lever that lets you shut the drinking tube with one hand.

lines.source: 我原先容易把不漏水，全想成嘴邊那一小塊；可是補水蓋，也是一個得關好的接面。
lines.text: I used to think keeping water in was all about that tiny piece at the mouth. But the refill cap is another joint that has to close properly.

lines.source: 如果出口沒有滴，水卻從蓋邊跑出來，你會先看哪裡？
lines.text: If the outlet is not dripping but water escapes around the cap, where would you look first?

lines.source: 原廠現行問答列出兩個可能原因：蓋子螺紋有砂粒，或者蓋內的密封圈扭了。
lines.text: The maker's current FAQ lists two possible causes: grit in the cap threads, or a twisted sealing ring inside the cap.

lines.source: 砂粒讓蓋子不能完整密合；那個黑色環若扭曲變形，也會破壞蓋口的密封。
lines.text: Grit prevents the cap from sealing fully. If that black ring twists out of shape, it can also compromise the seal.

lines.source: 能不能在背出去以前，讓這條縫先露出來？
lines.text: Can you expose that gap before carrying the bag outside?

lines.source: 原廠的季前檢查，把水裝回袋子，蓋好後轉動、擠壓，觀察有沒有漏水。
lines.text: For its pre-season check, the maker says to fill the reservoir, close the cap, then rotate and squeeze it while watching for leaks.

lines.source: 我覺得，它沒有離開一開始的問題：讓水跟你走，還得知道它有沒有從別的地方先走掉。
lines.text: I think it stays with our original question: to take water with you, you also need to know whether it has already escaped somewhere else.

lines.source: 可喝完、洗完之後，水反而不該再留在袋裡；這次要怎麼讓它出去？
lines.text: But after drinking and washing, water should no longer remain inside. How do you get it out this time?

lines.source: 洗後殘水，把水路反過來考了一次；原廠清潔頁說，角落、飲水管和咬口都可能留水。
lines.text: Water left after washing tests the route in reverse. The maker's cleaning page says water may remain in corners, the drinking tube and the bite valve.

lines.source: 你看到外面已經乾了，不表示管內和接縫，也一起乾了。
lines.text: Seeing a dry outside does not mean the inside of the tube and the seams have dried too.

lines.source: 我覺得這是整段水路最刁鑽的反面：喝的時候要留住水，收起來以前，卻要把殘水送走。
lines.text: To me, this is the trickiest reversal in the whole route: keep water in while drinking, but get the remaining water out before storage.

lines.source: 原廠的清洗範圍，因此不只是一個大袋子；水走過的管與咬口，也得接到清水。
lines.text: So the maker's cleaning guidance covers more than the large bag. The tube and mouthpiece that carried water need clean water too.

lines.source: 但洗掉殘留物以後，內壁還貼在一起，空氣要從哪裡進去？
lines.text: But after the residue is washed away, if the inner walls still stick together, where can air get in?

lines.source: 清潔頁給的動作，是把袋體撐開，讓內部通風；乾燥架把兩邊內壁分開，也讓水能排出。
lines.text: The cleaning page says to prop the reservoir open for ventilation. A drying rack separates the two inner walls and lets water drain.

lines.source: 飲水管若緊緊盤起來，原廠說水可能積在低處；怎麼讓管內也有乾燥的路？
lines.text: The maker says water may collect at low points if the tube is tightly coiled. How can you give the tube a route to dry too?

lines.source: 它排掉管裡的水，垂直掛起，並讓兩端敞開；乾燥不只留給袋子的內部。
lines.text: It drains the tube, hangs it vertically and leaves both ends open. Drying is not just for the reservoir's interior.

lines.source: 分件晾乾用到的是可拆零件；管與咬口各自留出的空間，也讓你能查看裡面是不是還有水。
lines.text: Drying the pieces separately uses removable parts. The space left for the tube and valve also lets you check whether water is still inside.

lines.source: 再看一眼，才知道能不能收回去；原廠要你看的是什麼？
lines.text: One more look tells you whether it can be stored. What does the maker want you to check?

lines.source: 原廠要求收存前再看接縫、角落、管子和接口，有沒有水滴或凝結；還有水，就繼續晾乾。
lines.text: Before storage, the maker asks you to check seams, corners, tubes and connections for droplets or condensation. If water remains, keep drying.

lines.source: 開場問水能不能留在該在的地方，到這裡，答案多了一個時間點：收起來時，它得離開。
lines.text: We began by asking whether water can stay where it belongs. Here, the answer gains another moment: when you store it, the water must leave.

lines.source: 一袋水的方便，是把開、關與重新使用接成水路；容量留在背上，出口和接縫，卻都得被照顧。
lines.text: A bag of water becomes convenient when opening, closing and reuse form a connected route. The capacity sits on your back, but the outlets and joints still need care.

lines.source: 你最常把水帶去騎車、走路，還是放在桌邊？留言告訴我，哪個小地方最讓你在意。
lines.text: Do you most often take water cycling, walking, or keep it by your desk? Tell me in the comments which small detail matters most to you.

lines.source: 想知道熟悉的物品，怎麼把方便送到你手裡，歡迎訂閱，和我一起看那些真正起作用的小動作。
lines.text: To see how familiar objects bring convenience to your hands, subscribe and join me in looking at the small actions that make them work.
